name: SMU
summary: Defending ACC champions, and the one big-name school where CS isn't gated.
verdict: Blue-chip soccer, elite teaching ratios, unrestricted CS. The cost is the barrier at nearly $70,000.

name: UCF
questionnaire: Recruit Questionnaire in the men's soccer nav
summary: Reigning Sun Belt champions who beat Kentucky and Marshall on the road to get there.
verdict: Cheap, warm, winning, and one flight from Toronto. The class sizes are the honest cost.

name: USF
summary: The strongest MLS pipeline on the list, mid-rebuild with 22 newcomers.
verdict: A brand-new staff rebuilding from scratch is the most open door on the Core 12 — and the most uncertain.

name: South Carolina
summary: Ranked No. 6 nationally, and the best crowds in American college soccer.
verdict: A top-six program, the best atmosphere in the country, the top-ranked international business degree, and forgiving admissions. The airport is the only real weakness.

name: Ohio State
summary: Best-balanced school on the list — top-five soccer, top-15 public, three hours from the border.
verdict: If one school has to balance soccer, academics and travel, this is it.

name: Penn State
summary: A Canadian national-championship coach in year one of a rebuild.
verdict: Highest-upside situation on the Core 12. A championship coach who needs players will give minutes — if you can absorb a three-year rebuild.

name: Boston University
summary: Best teaching ratio on the list, and the most reachable coaching staff.
verdict: Small classes, real soccer, an easy staff to contact. The price and the admission rate are the gates.

name: Northeastern
summary: Strongest academics on either list, weakest soccer on the Core 12. That trade is the whole story.
verdict: If soccer is the route into an institution otherwise out of reach, this is the clearest example of that trade anywhere here.

name: UC Santa Barbara
summary: The only national champion here — and the only school that fails the business requirement outright.
verdict: The best soccer pedigree available — unless a business degree is a requirement, in which case it's out.

name: NJIT
summary: Best financial outcome on the Core 12, and the best airport access.
verdict: Best return on investment here, if the subject fit is right and you can finish the degree.

name: UMass Lowell
summary: Easiest door on the Core 12, and closer to the border than either Boston school.
verdict: The value and access play. Modest soccer, cheap housing, and a realistic drive home.

name: IU Indianapolis
summary: A defensive side that scores from penalties — ideal for a defender, a question mark for a forward.
verdict: Cheapest option with the second-best teaching ratio. The graduation and earnings numbers are the honest counterweight.

name: FIU
summary: Cheapest out-of-state tuition in the entire research, by a wide margin.
verdict: If cost is a live constraint, this reshapes the list. Verify international rates separately.

name: Georgia State
summary: Seventeen years of coaching stability and the best airport on either list.
verdict: Buy the coaching stability and the airport. Confirm what campus life actually looks like.

name: Kennesaw State
head_coach: Not found — call the athletics department
summary: Program confirmed to exist, but no public information about it. Phone them.
verdict: Cheap and confirmed, but unknowable from a desk. Low priority until you've spoken to someone there.

name: NC State
summary: 2025 national runners-up, picked first in the ACC, and cheaper than most of the Core 12.
verdict: Arguably the best soccer-per-dollar on the whole list, with Boston-level internship density next door.

name: UNC Chapel Hill
summary: The best combination of soccer and academics anywhere here — and the hardest door to open.
verdict: Worth pursuing precisely because athletics is the one route in. Have the admissions conversation with the staff before investing.

name: UNC Charlotte
summary: Possibly the strongest value combination in the entire research.
verdict: A winning program, forgiving admission, low cost, ten hours from home, direct flights. The only gap is the blocked staff directory.

name: Florida Atlantic
summary: Lowest net price in the research, attached to a program that just broke through.
verdict: Cheapest realistic option once aid is counted, on a rising program that recruits Canadians. Contacts still need gathering.

name: Clemson
summary: The best professional pathway in college soccer right now.
verdict: If professional soccer is the goal and $60,000 is absorbable, this is the strongest case anywhere. If not, Charlotte gives you most of it for a third.

name: Georgia Southern
summary: Easiest admission in the research, attached to a team that was ranked sixth nationally.
verdict: Ranked sixth in the country last year and you can get in with an 88% admit rate. The open question is whether 2025 was a step change or a spike.

name: Nova Southeastern
summary: A heavily international squad — but a small undergraduate college inside a health-professions university.
verdict: The international roster is a real positive. Everything else points elsewhere unless marine science appeals.

name: Keiser
summary: Excellent soccer at a 1,500-student career college. NAIA eligibility rules are the useful part.
verdict: Great soccer, wrong academics. Worth knowing for the NAIA eligibility route more than the school itself.

name: UNC Wilmington
summary: The clearest evidence anywhere that freshmen actually play.
verdict: If early minutes matter more than the badge, this is the strongest evidence on the list. Check the international tuition first.

name: UNC Greensboro
summary: Ranked last by size, and one of the four or five best soccer programs in this entire research.
verdict: The biggest mismatch here between soccer quality and list position. If soccer per dollar is the criterion, this belongs near the top.

name: University of Toronto
summary: The oldest program in this research, in a rebuild year with nine starters gone.
verdict: The strongest academic institution available at domestic prices, mid-rebuild, with a coach openly looking to younger players.

name: York University
summary: Reigning national champions, with a roster built from MLS Next Pro and League1 Ontario.
verdict: If the Canadian route is live at all, this is the first call.

name: Western University
summary: Best traditional campus of the three — but the head coach runs two programs at once.
verdict: Best campus experience of the three. The divided coaching role and the two-year Ivey pathway are the questions to resolve.
